artifacts.summary: Repaired buildContextExpr's List.nil arity defect, moved both Search.lean call sites inside their observing? blocks, and added an invoked MetaM probe plus three modal_search acceptance examples.

completion_data.completion_summary: buildContextExpr's nil case now builds via mkAppOptM ``List.nil #[some formulaType] instead of passing List.nil's implicit type parameter explicitly to mkAppM, which had made it throw on every input including the empty list. Both consumers in Search.lean (tryModalK, tryTemporalK) now call it inside their observing? blocks, so an elaboration failure there is a failed search branch rather than a hard tactic error. Tests/BimodalTest/Automation/LemmaDBTest.lean gained an invoked MetaM probe pinning buildContextExpr's output against Meta.mkListLit on the empty and a two-element list, plus three modal_search acceptance examples (box-headed at empty and non-empty all-boxed contexts, and allFuture-headed); the box-headed one was measured red pre-repair.

sapience_notes.subject: Lean 4 mkAppM vs mkAppOptM for a declaration with implicit leading arguments
sapience_notes.value: mkAppM's Array Expr fills only EXPLICIT parameters, so passing a type argument for List.nil (whose type parameter is implicit) raises 'too many explicit arguments provided to @List.nil' on every input, the empty list included. mkAppOptM takes Array (Option Expr) and assigns each `some` entry to the next parameter whether implicit or explicit, so `mkAppOptM ``List.nil #[some formulaType]` is the correct form. The defect type-checks and builds clean because the error is raised at elaborator RUNTIME, not at compile time.

sapience_notes.subject: Covering a MetaM helper with #check in a Lean test suite
sapience_notes.value: A #check on a MetaM helper is not coverage and can mask a total defect indefinitely. #check pins only the declaration's type (here `List Expr -> MetaM Expr`), which is unchanged by any AppBuilder arity mistake in the body; the mistake surfaces only when the function is actually applied. BimodalLogic's buildContextExpr threw on 100% of inputs while `lake build` and `lake test` were exit-0 with zero warnings, because the only coverage was a #check and no test reached its consumers. An invoked #eval probe is what a MetaM helper owes; it runs at elaboration time, so a failed assertion surfaces as a build error.

sapience_notes.subject: Placing a speculative elaboration call relative to Lean's observing? block
sapience_notes.value: A call that can throw during a speculative search branch belongs INSIDE the observing? block, not above it. In BimodalLogic's tryModalK/tryTemporalK the buildContextExpr call sat above the block, so its exception propagated and aborted modal_search entirely instead of registering as a failed branch. Moving it inside is safe whenever the call reads no goal state, since observing?'s state rollback on failure is then harmless. Side effect worth knowing: the move strands a blank line above `let success <- observing? do`, which Mathlib's standard linter rejects as 'do not place empty lines within commands' and which fails a --wfail build.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic's typst-sync-check.sh --fix coverage of generated surfaces
sapience_notes.value: typst-sync-check.sh --fix repairs typst/generated/status.typ ONLY. Its Check 2b reports drift in typst/generated/automation-module-map.typ but is read-only and prints 'regenerate via: bash scripts/typst-module-map.sh', which is a separate regenerator that must be run by hand. A .lean edit changing a module's raw line count therefore drifts at least three generated surfaces (status.typ, automation-module-map.typ, and the inventory block that check-module-invariants.sh --emit-inventory owns), each with its own regenerator.

sapience_notes.subject: lean-plan-compliance-check.sh on a plan that names a Lean tactic
sapience_notes.value: The script's per-name matcher greps for declaration keywords (def/theorem/lemma/instance), so any plan-harvested identifier that is declared as tactic SYNTAX rather than as a declaration is reported [MISSING] and flips the whole run to COMPLIANCE_CHECK: failed. BimodalLogic's modal_search is declared `syntax "modal_search" (num)? : tactic`, so it reports missing while compiling fine in `example ... := by modal_search`. This is a false-positive class alongside the dotted-token and structure-field classes the script's own header already documents; do not downgrade a task's status on it without checking how the named identifier is declared.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-touched.sh scope derivation on a shared, concurrently-dispatched working tree
sapience_notes.value: verify-touched.sh derives its touched-path set from the whole working tree, so other sessions' uncommitted specs/TODO.md, specs/state.json and specs/events.jsonl edits are attributed to the running dispatch and pull in the entire agent-system test battery regardless of what the dispatch actually edited. In BimodalLogic, which is a deploy-only tree with no on-disk agent-system/ source store, that battery contributes a standing ~11-of-95 suite failure (e.g. test-generate-task-order.sh: 'generate-task-order.sh not found (mode=source-store)'). Read such failures as a baseline property and check whether any failing suite reads a file the dispatch edited before treating them as a regression.
